name: Yahboom DOFBOT Pro / Ultra
description: A 6-axis desktop robot arm kit built around a single-board computer (Jetson Nano in the version pictured) and an onboard camera, marketed for AI vision education — color/gesture/face tracking, object detection, and pick-and-place demos taught through Yahboom's own Python/OpenCV/ROS curriculum. Sold as one product family across several compute-board variants rather than a single fixed SKU.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: Jetson Nano generation figure; requires 12V/5A power supply

specs.label: Compute (current)
specs.note: Pro: Jetson Nano/Orin Nano/Orin NX; Ultra: Raspberry Pi 5 or RDK X5

specs.label: Camera (current)
specs.note: Pro and Ultra both ship a depth camera, a step up from the original's 0.3MP unit

specs.label: Software
specs.note: Ultra adds ROS2 and vision-guided grasping; OpenCV/YOLOv5/MediaPipe referenced in course materials

specs.label: Degrees of Freedom
specs.note: 5 arm joints (servos 1–5, base rotation hidden at the mount) + 1 gripper axis (servo 6)

specs.label: Payload
specs.note: ~200g fully extended — third-party spec for the original Jetson Nano version, not on Yahboom's own sheet

specs.label: Actuators
specs.note: 5× 15kg·cm + 1× 6kg·cm gripper servo; exact branded model number not published

sourcing: Specs compiled from Yahboom's own product and GitHub pages for the Jetson Nano DOFBOT, independent hardware coverage from CNX Software (payload, reach, weight, camera resolution), and NVIDIA's official Jetson product lifecycle page (Jetson Nano EOL status), as of this build. Exact servo model/part number, precise release date, and current third-party (Amazon/RobotShop) pricing could not be independently confirmed and are described only in general terms above. "Open source" is Yahboom's own marketing language, not a confirmed license grant — the GitHub repos have no LICENSE file. The current DOFBOT Pro and DOFBOT Ultra lines and their pricing are confirmed via Yahboom's own category pages (category.yahboom.net), RobotShop, and OpenELAB listings; this entry's display name and lead specs have been updated to reflect them as Yahboom's current models, while the original Jetson Nano hardware specs above (weight, payload, camera resolution, reach) describe the entry-level SKU pictured, not the Pro/Ultra lines.

pricing.summary: Yahboom's current lineup has moved past the original Jetson Nano DOFBOT pictured here (still listed at $339, alongside a $329 Raspberry Pi–based DOFBOT-Pi) to two newer lines: **DOFBOT Pro**, from $499 with Jetson Nano/Orin Nano/Orin NX compute options, and **DOFBOT Ultra**, from $349 with Raspberry Pi 5 or RDK X5 compute and an "AI Large Language Model" 3D-depth-vision pitch. It's also resold on Amazon, RobotShop, Newegg, and OpenELAB, but current third-party pricing wasn't independently verifiable, so treat Yahboom's own listed prices as the more reliable figures.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Despite "open source" language in Yahboom's marketing, the Jetson Nano DOFBOT's GitHub repo carries no LICENSE file and shows no published releases — no Open Source badge is applied here. Payload, reach, and repeatability figures come from independent hardware coverage rather than Yahboom's own spec sheet, and haven't been corroborated by a second source. This page originally covered only the older Jetson Nano version pictured here; Yahboom's current lineup has since moved on to two parallel successor lines, both centered on 3D depth vision and marketed AI features: **DOFBOT Pro** (Jetson Nano/Orin Nano/Orin NX compute, from $499) and **DOFBOT Ultra** (Raspberry Pi 5 or RDK X5 compute, from $349, with an "AI Large Language Model" pitch and ROS2/vision-guided grasping). The original Jetson Nano DOFBOT still appears to be sold at $339, but it's now the entry-level option rather than Yahboom's featured model.

firmwareCommunity.note: Yahboom's official GitHub repo for the Jetson Nano DOFBOT has real, actively-committed Python/ROS code, though it carries no LICENSE file, so usage rights are not formally granted.
